## When to use

Choose a topology, conservative-transfer, ordered-channel or camera-georeferencing operation; preserve explicit CRS and coordinate conventions.

## Required inputs

Load only the selected tool's closed schema. Use its synthetic asset as an input-shape example, not a real observation. Units are mandatory literal dictionaries. Raster origin is the upper-left outer corner; rows run north to south. Landlab guard nodes are boundaries, not extra model cells. Geometry is 2D and metric; no silent reprojection or repair.

## Workflow

1. Establish the scientific task, input units, CRS, physical domain and boundary conditions.
2. Choose one matching entry below, rather than running the entire tool list.
3. Check private-environment availability and stage the catalog before invoking the shared decorator.
4. Inspect output masks, units and provenance. For modelling steps, assess the explicitly described stability and mass-balance limits.
5. Hand off to independent CPU acceptance before scientific use or registration. Model/lab/platform acceptance is not established.

## Tool contracts

### GeoSpatialCoverageSimplification

Simplify internal boundaries of an edge-matched polygon coverage without simplifying its outer boundary.

Fixed upstream: `shapely.coverage_simplify` (shapely==2.1.2).

Input example: `assets/expansion501-spatial/GeoSpatialCoverageSimplification.json` (synthetic).

Constraints: GEOS >=3.12 mandatory (parent baseline 3.13.1); valid 2D coverage; tolerance is Visvalingam square-root-area metric, not Hausdorff displacement.

Independent numeric acceptance plan: Two adjacent unit squares stay a gap-free partition with total area 2 m2 and unchanged outer boundary; shared edge coordinates agree in both polygons.

Distinctness: Generic GeoShapelyGeometry per-feature simplify can break coverage topology; this calls the coverage-aware algorithm with boundary preservation.

Source: https://github.com/shapely/shapely/blob/5fb639d1056888d135fe56bfaf750c9648addeec/shapely/_coverage.py

### GeoSpatialConservativeArealTransfer

Transfer extensive totals between complete polygon partitions by intersection-area allocation.

Fixed upstream: `tobler.area_weighted.area_interpolate` (tobler==0.14.0).

Input example: `assets/expansion501-spatial/GeoSpatialConservativeArealTransfer.json` (synthetic).

Constraints: Identical footprint and internally nonoverlapping partitions; allocate_total=False; homogeneous density within each source polygon; no uncovered-area redistribution.

Independent numeric acceptance plan: Totals 100 and 200 kg on two equal-area source rectangles, each bisected: target totals [50,50,100,100], global mass 300 kg.

Distinctness: Exact raster zonal statistics aggregates samples under polygons; this conservatively redistributes polygon extensive quantities between nonmatching partitions.

Source: https://github.com/pysal/tobler/blob/955790dac77f4a76d06591ffe9f246cfb0af4501/tobler/area_weighted/area_interpolate.py

### GeoSpatialRPCGeolocation

Geolocate image pixel centres using a rational polynomial camera and explicit ellipsoidal heights.

Fixed upstream: `rasterio.transform.RPCTransformer.xy` (rasterio==1.4.3).

Input example: `assets/expansion501-spatial/GeoSpatialRPCGeolocation.json` (synthetic).

Constraints: No DEM URL or arbitrary GDAL options; height inside normalization range; inverse warnings become errors; output CRS explicitly EPSG:4326, never the pixel source.

Independent numeric acceptance plan: Synthetic linear RPC line=P,sample=L with all offsets zero and scales one: pixel centre row=col=0 at ellipsoid height 0 gives lon=lat=0. Off-centre sample explicitly checks GDAL pixel-centre convention.

Distinctness: Raster reprojection assumes existing spatial georeferencing; RPC inversion resolves camera geometry and height-dependent pixel-to-ground positions.

Source: https://github.com/rasterio/rasterio/blob/7f8bda2e32df5b5eefc6e1ea6b5f04a946567ede/rasterio/transform.py

### GeoSpatialGCPGeoreferencing

Fit a thin-plate-spline ground-control transformation and locate in-hull image coordinates.

Fixed upstream: `rasterio.transform.GCPTransformer.xy` (rasterio==1.4.3).

Input example: `assets/expansion501-spatial/GeoSpatialGCPGeoreferencing.json` (synthetic).

Constraints: At least four distinct noncollinear controls; only interpolation in pixel convex hull; no Z/M or CRS conversion; corner convention explicit.

Independent numeric acceptance plan: Affine-compatible controls x=100+2*col,y=200-3*row are reproduced exactly by TPS; row=col=5 -> (110,185) m.

Distinctness: Affine geotransform/raster reprojection cannot infer a non-affine georeferencing surface from irregular GCPs; fixed TPS, not another coordinate component tool.

Source: https://github.com/rasterio/rasterio/blob/7f8bda2e32df5b5eefc6e1ea6b5f04a946567ede/rasterio/transform.py

### GeoSpatialLineworkPolygonTopology

Extract polygons and diagnose cut edges, dangles and invalid rings from noded linework.

Fixed upstream: `shapely.polygonize_full` (shapely==2.1.2).

Input example: `assets/expansion501-spatial/GeoSpatialLineworkPolygonTopology.json` (synthetic).

Constraints: Input linework must already be noded for intended topology; crossings are not split/snapped automatically; valid individual 2D LineStrings.

Independent numeric acceptance plan: Four unit-square edges plus one spur: exactly one polygon of area 1 m2 and one dangle; no cut edges or invalid rings.

Distinctness: Generic polygon union/geometry repair is not a full graph polygonization diagnostic; four explicit topology categories are returned without repair.

Source: https://github.com/shapely/shapely/blob/5fb639d1056888d135fe56bfaf750c9648addeec/shapely/constructive.py

### GeoSpatialChannelFrechetDeviation

Measure ordered centreline deviation using the discrete Frechet distance.

Fixed upstream: `shapely.frechet_distance` (shapely==2.1.2).

Input example: `assets/expansion501-spatial/GeoSpatialChannelFrechetDeviation.json` (synthetic).

Constraints: 2D projected metric LineStrings; no automatic reversal/densification; sample-vertex dependent, not continuous Frechet.

Independent numeric acceptance plan: Parallel 10 m lines separated by 2 m have discrete Frechet=2 m; reversing the second line gives sqrt(104) m, establishing traversal-order sensitivity.

Distinctness: Hausdorff/nearest geometry proximity ignores traversal order; discrete Frechet respects ordered channel correspondence.

Source: https://github.com/shapely/shapely/blob/5fb639d1056888d135fe56bfaf750c9648addeec/shapely/measurement.py

Upscale a D8 drainage network using iterative hydrography-preserving IHU.

Distinctness: Existing D8 accumulation/delineation/Strahler tools retain grid resolution; IHU constructs a topologically consistent coarser network.

Source: https://github.com/Deltares/pyflwdir/blob/4e598e77611232bbf5fc620919d914de5bfd2cdb/pyflwdir/pyflwdir.py

### GeoSpatialFloodplainStageStorage

Calculate subcatchment flood storage-volume curves from prescribed HAND and stages.

Fixed upstream: `pyflwdir.pyflwdir.FlwdirRaster.ucat_volume` (pyflwdir==0.5.12).

Input example: `assets/expansion501-spatial/GeoSpatialFloodplainStageStorage.json` (synthetic).

Source: https://github.com/Deltares/pyflwdir/blob/4e598e77611232bbf5fc620919d914de5bfd2cdb/pyflwdir/pyflwdir.py

### GeoSpatialChannelChiCoordinate

Integrate the channel chi coordinate using true D8 link lengths and a fixed reference concavity.

Fixed upstream: `landlab.components.ChiFinder.calculate_chi` (landlab==2.11.0).

Input example: `assets/expansion501-spatial/GeoSpatialChannelChiCoordinate.json` (synthetic).

Constraints: Reference concavity=.5; use_true_dx=True; output null exactly at upstream hillslope mask, distinct from input NoData; routing unchanged and no depressions filled.

Independent numeric acceptance plan: Independent path integral: when all contributing path nodes have A=A0, chi increments equal physical path lengths; a two-link 1 m path is chi=2 m. Also chi scales as sqrt(A0) with fixed area/routing. Masks must exclude nonchannels rather than report them as valid zero.

Distinctness: Drainage distance is unweighted path length; chi integrates (A0/A)^.5 and normalizes longitudinal profiles by drainage area.

Source: https://github.com/landlab/landlab/blob/575b4b7b424e9c74c55fc5cf334fbec6bea92723/src/landlab/components/chi_index/channel_chi.py

Distinctness: Least-cost/drainage routing follows topography without momentum or storage; this solves dynamic shallow-water flux/depth for one bounded physical step.

### GeoSpatialGroundwaterZoneBudget

Aggregate cell-by-cell MODFLOW flux records into inter-zone groundwater water budgets.

Input example: `assets/expansion501-spatial/GeoSpatialGroundwaterZoneBudget.json` (synthetic).

Distinctness: Not MODFLOW execution, hydraulic interpolation or polygon zonal statistics; conserves signed intercell and source/sink fluxes across model zones.

Source: https://github.com/modflowpy/flopy/blob/a43f79127d0383e5328a602e72faf9a9730c7d61/flopy/utils/zonbud.py

### GeoSpatialDarcySpecificDischarge

Convert fully saturated model face volumetric fluxes to Darcy specific discharge on each staggered face.

Fixed upstream: `flopy.utils.postprocessing.get_specific_discharge` (flopy==3.11.0).

Input example: `assets/expansion501-spatial/GeoSpatialDarcySpecificDischarge.json` (synthetic).

Constraints: Fully saturated active cells only; explicit extended face arrays; rows north-to-south, layers top-to-bottom; no implicit south/down sign conversion; no MODFLOW executable.

Independent numeric acceptance plan: dx=2 m, thickness=5 m: side areas 10 m2 and horizontal area 4 m2; Qeast=20,Qnorth=30,Qup=16 m3/s yield q=(2,3,4) m/s on all faces.

Distinctness: Hydraulic-gradient/flow solvers do not convert existing cell-budget face fluxes using saturated cross-sectional geometry; this is postprocessing, not generic vector decomposition.

Source: https://github.com/modflowpy/flopy/blob/a43f79127d0383e5328a602e72faf9a9730c7d61/flopy/utils/postprocessing.py

### GeoSpatialScreenedTransmissivity

Calculate layer-specific saturated transmissivity intersecting screened well intervals.

Fixed upstream: `flopy.utils.postprocessing.get_transmissivities` (flopy==3.11.0).

Input example: `assets/expansion501-spatial/GeoSpatialScreenedTransmissivity.json` (synthetic).

Constraints: Screens entirely inside model; reject dry layers and nonintersecting screens to avoid upstream closest-layer fallback; no well-loss or pumping-test inversion.

Independent numeric acceptance plan: Two 5 m saturated screened layers, K=[.01,.002] m/s: transmissivities [.05,.01] m2/s and total .06 m2/s; shortened 3 m first-layer interval gives .03 m2/s.

Distinctness: Not scalar transmissivity multiplication alone: intersects multilayer geology, well screen and saturation heads at explicit model cells.

Source: https://github.com/modflowpy/flopy/blob/a43f79127d0383e5328a602e72faf9a9730c7d61/flopy/utils/postprocessing.py

Advance shallow unconfined groundwater storage with the Dupuit-percolator approximation.

Fixed upstream: `landlab.components.GroundwaterDupuitPercolator.run_one_step` (landlab==2.11.0).

Input example: `assets/expansion501-spatial/GeoSpatialUnconfinedGroundwaterStep.json` (synthetic).

Independent numeric acceptance plan: Flat closed aquifer with uniform 2 m head, base 0, land 10 and no recharge remains head=2 m and thickness=2 m exactly; no lateral gradient gives zero transport.

Distinctness: Darcy postprocessing and well transmissivity are static analyses; this evolves distributed unconfined storage with recharge and nonlinear saturated thickness.

Source: https://github.com/landlab/landlab/blob/575b4b7b424e9c74c55fc5cf334fbec6bea92723/src/landlab/components/groundwater/dupuit_percolator.py

### GeoSpatialLocalHeteroscedasticity

Measure local spatial variation in residual dispersion with LOSH, without permutation inference.

Fixed upstream: `esda.losh.LOSH.fit` (esda==2.10.0).

Input example: `assets/expansion501-spatial/GeoSpatialLocalHeteroscedasticity.json` (synthetic).

Constraints: Symmetric supplied binary adjacency, no islands/self edges; nonconstant data; a=2; inference=None; no p-value or significance claim.

Independent numeric acceptance plan: Binary-weight four-node chain with y=[0,0,0,2]: local means [0,0,1,0], squared residuals [0,0,1,4], global mean 1.25; Hi=[0,.4,1.6,.8].

Distinctness: Local Moran/Getis-Ord measure value clustering; LOSH measures spatial heterogeneity of residual variance, not another autocorrelation alias.

Source: https://github.com/pysal/esda/blob/6ffd5b66565791cede8703c438c90a819aacd49f/esda/losh.py

### GeoSpatialContiguousRegionalization

Partition an explicit connected spatial adjacency graph into attribute-homogeneous contiguous regions with SKATER.

Fixed upstream: `spopt.region.Skater.solve` (spopt==0.8.0).

Input example: `assets/expansion501-spatial/GeoSpatialContiguousRegionalization.json` (synthetic).

Constraints: Commensurate dimensionless features; L1 default objective; strictly positive adjacent dissimilarities avoid sparse zero-edge deletion; no MILP or global optimum claim.

Independent numeric acceptance plan: Four-node chain features [0,1,10,11], two regions of at least two: only feasible connected split [0,0,1,1], within-region absolute deviations total 2.

Distinctness: DBSCAN/site proximity need not yield a chosen number of adjacency-contiguous regions; this optimizes a spanning-tree regionalization heuristic with region-size constraints.

Source: https://github.com/pysal/spopt/blob/8d282940ab2827f84cb5f8319e396aa90ac686aa/spopt/region/skater.py

### GeoSpatialKnoxSpaceTimeInteraction

Count joint spatial-temporal event proximity and its contingency expectation using Knox.

Input example: `assets/expansion501-spatial/GeoSpatialKnoxSpaceTimeInteraction.json` (synthetic).

Constraints: Metric XY and common-epoch seconds; permutations=0; duplicate events represent separate records and are not dropped.

Independent numeric acceptance plan: Three events at x=[0,1,10] and t=[0,1,10], thresholds 2: one of three unordered pairs is jointly close; independent-margin expected joint count=1/3.

Distinctness: Pure spatial Moran/K/Ripley and temporal anomaly tools do not test joint event-pair space-time proximity; here only observed counts and expectations, not stochastic inference.

Source: https://github.com/pysal/pointpats/blob/524296c551488998a26000c072d69b76ca095d68/pointpats/spacetime.py

### GeoSpatialRipleyKObservedWindow

Estimate uncorrected Ripley K for point events using their observed bounding rectangle.

### GeoSpatialHillslopeDiffusionStep

Advance a gridded hillslope by one linear soil-creep diffusion step.

Fixed upstream: `landlab.components.LinearDiffuser.run_one_step` (landlab==2.11.0).

Input example: `assets/expansion501-spatial/GeoSpatialHillslopeDiffusionStep.json` (synthetic).

Constraints: One explicit method=simple/deposit=True step; dt*K/dx^2<=.2; all boundary nodes fixed to input, finite complete grid, at most 1024 nodes.

Independent numeric acceptance plan: Synthetic z=x^2+y^2 on 1 m grid: central 2D Laplacian=4; K=.1 m2/s,dt=.1 s -> centre elevation increase .04 m. Fixed guard nodes unchanged.

Distinctness: Terrain slope/curvature are diagnostics; this advances a PDE governing hillslope mass redistribution, not a derivative alias.

Source: https://github.com/landlab/landlab/blob/575b4b7b424e9c74c55fc5cf334fbec6bea92723/src/landlab/components/diffusion/diffusion.py

### GeoSpatialStreamPowerErosionStep

Advance detachment-limited stream-power incision with implicit Fastscape on fixed D8 drainage.

Fixed upstream: `landlab.components.FastscapeEroder.run_one_step` (landlab==2.11.0).

Input example: `assets/expansion501-spatial/GeoSpatialStreamPowerErosionStep.json` (synthetic).

Constraints: Fixed m=.5,n=1,threshold=0, K s^-1; D8 FlowAccumulator runoff_rate=1; no pit filling, uplift, transport or calibration; fixed boundaries.

Independent numeric acceptance plan: Synthetic one-core-node 3x3 DEM: centre z=1, west fixed outlet z=0, all other neighbors z=2, dx=1,A=1,K=.1,dt=1 -> implicit z_new=1/(1+.1)=10/11 m. Guard nodes unchanged.

Distinctness: Existing flow direction/accumulation produce routing only; fixed routing is a prerequisite here for a physically dimensioned fluvial-incision time step.

Source: https://github.com/landlab/landlab/blob/575b4b7b424e9c74c55fc5cf334fbec6bea92723/src/landlab/components/stream_power/fastscape_stream_power.py

### GeoMarineCarbonateAccretion

Advance spatial biogenic carbonate accretion under light attenuation in a fully submerged environment.

Fixed upstream: `landlab.components.CarbonateProducer.run_one_step` (landlab==2.11.0).

Input example: `assets/expansion501-spatial/GeoMarineCarbonateAccretion.json` (synthetic).

Constraints: m/year and years, light in microEinstein/m2/s; tidal_range=0 fixed; fully submerged throughout step; empirical ecology not a field-calibrated forecast.

Independent numeric acceptance plan: Uniform 10 m water depth: rate=.01*tanh(5*exp(-1)) m/year; dt=1 gives that thickness at each core. Surface light=0 gives exactly zero accretion. Outer nodes unchanged.

Distinctness: Biogenic sediment production is neither equilibrium mineral chemistry nor mechanical sediment erosion; this is a spatial depositional-evolution law.

Source: https://github.com/landlab/landlab/blob/575b4b7b424e9c74c55fc5cf334fbec6bea92723/src/landlab/components/carbonate/carbonate_producer.py

### GeoRegolithProductionRate

Compute soil-thickness-shielded bedrock-to-regolith production rates.

Fixed upstream: `landlab.components.ExponentialWeatherer.calc_soil_prod_rate` (landlab==2.11.0).

Input example: `assets/expansion501-spatial/GeoRegolithProductionRate.json` (synthetic).

Constraints: Landlab ExponentialWeatherer exact law, scalar calibration; output rate not timestep evolution; boundary values explicitly masked as undefined model rates.

Independent numeric acceptance plan: At H=0, H=Hstar and H=2Hstar, rates W0, W0/e and W0/e^2; e.g. W0=.01 m/year, Hstar=1 m gives .0036787944117 at H=1.

Distinctness: Terrain metrics and empirical chemical weathering indices do not calculate a thickness-dependent regolith-production field used by landscape models.

Source: https://github.com/landlab/landlab/blob/575b4b7b424e9c74c55fc5cf334fbec6bea92723/src/landlab/components/weathering/exponential_weathering.py

### GeoLithosphereFlexure

Calculate two-dimensional elastic lithospheric flexure from a gridded pressure increment.

Fixed upstream: `landlab.components.Flexure.update` (landlab==2.11.0).

Input example: `assets/expansion501-spatial/GeoLithosphereFlexure.json` (synthetic).

Constraints: Fixed method=flexure, n_procs=1, positive-down deflection, positive pressure loads, infinite elastic plate with zero loads beyond sampled rectangle; at most 256 nodes; no Airy mode alias.

Independent numeric acceptance plan: Zero load produces exactly zero deflection. For a single point-cell force F=p*dx^2: centre w(0)=F/(8*rho*g*alpha^2), alpha=(D/(rho*g))^(1/4), D=E*Te^3/[12*(1-.25^2)]; verify alpha definition against pinned component and isotropic symmetry.

Distinctness: Gravity forward modeling calculates acceleration from density; elastic flexure calculates mechanical plate displacement from applied load, not a gravity alias or slope-stability solver.

Source: https://github.com/landlab/landlab/blob/575b4b7b424e9c74c55fc5cf334fbec6bea92723/src/landlab/components/flexure/flexure.py

Advect a passive soil property with depth-dependent hillslope sediment diffusion and prescribed bedrock production.

Distinctness: Not a geochemical mixing/speciation wrapper: follows passive material concentration under spatially coupled hillslope flux and soil production.
